analysis:
Examined all supplied workflow, changelog, metadata and build-guide units. ci.yml head lines 1072–1074 and 1134–1136 add route dependencies and dynamic runner selection for GPU and focused cluster checks. The surrounding checkout retains pinned actions, persist-credentials:false, cache-save gating and bounded job/test timeouts. GPU test failures remain nonblocking (1122–1128), while the Provider Tests gate still requires selected blocking and focused lanes to succeed (1185–1217); these controls are not newly weakened here. The documentation patch and changelog lines 3–6 describe extending routing to macOS provider/cluster lanes with per-shard grants and Blacksmith fallback. Build-guide BASE lines 282–291 establish that these lanes previously used literal Blacksmith labels and record historical sandbox timeout experience; that history alone does not prove a current security regression.
The relevant integration concern is CI execution/cache integrity on provider-owned Macs (ADV-001, TB-003), particularly whether newly routed push jobs can seed artifacts consumed by trusted qualification/signing (A-011, A-017, T-054). No supplied evidence establishes a missing isolation control or a path to release compromise. Provider transport, authorization, encryption, billing and runtime secrecy controls (TB-002, TB-011) are not directly modified in this scope. Further integration must verify the route producer's exact-label validation, fork and branch admission, job token/secret scope, sandbox isolation and cache consumers against the complete workflow/action sources. The claims in build.md BASE 265–280 and 302–334 are documentation, not implementation proof. Preserve release qualification separation described at BASE 181–186 and 435–460; CI success does not establish native Apple or physical-host qualification. No independently supported finding in these units.
